{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study discusses the predictive validity of animal models of addiction for human clinical outcomes and provides examples of how animal model findings translate to human situations, such as the use of nalmefene in humans and opioid-receptor blockade in rats for alcohol consumption. It also discusses the translation of findings from the alcohol deprivation effect model to clinical situations with medications like naltrexone and acamprosate.",
  "arm": "efficacy",
  "arm_evidence": "For example, pharmacological opioid-receptor blockade reduces alcohol consumption in many self-administration studies in different strains of rats and mice under different conditions, which provides generalizability of preclinical data that translates to the human situation, in which the opioid-receptor blocker nalmefene also reduces alcohol consumption.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "psychiatric"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The text focuses on animal models of addiction, which is a psychiatric disorder, and discusses their relevance to human drug consumption and addiction.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The text discusses various animal models including self-administration-based models, nonoperant and operant procedures, reinstatement models, incubation of drug-seeking, and DSM-based models for alcohol and cocaine addiction.",
  "species": [
    "rat",
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The text explicitly mentions the use of laboratory animals such as monkeys, rats, and mice, and later discusses the differences and suitability of rats versus mice for addiction research.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study discusses various endpoints including drug consumption, motivation to self-administer drugs, relapse behavior, craving, and neurobiological mechanisms, which encompass both behavioral outcomes and underlying biological markers."
}
